original_question: What is the moduli space of left invariant affine connections on the statistical Lie group of univariate normal distributions that are compatible with the Fisher metric?
target_in_paper: Section 1 (Jun-ichi Inoguchi), item 1: "Determine the moduli space of left invariant affine connections on the statistical Lie group of univariate normal distributions compatible to the Fisher metric."
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the paper's target almost verbatim: it identifies the same model (the statistical Lie group of univariate normal distributions), the same class of objects (left invariant affine connections), and the same compatibility requirement with the Fisher metric. It also stays narrowly on the intended problem rather than drifting into broader information-geometric classification questions.
missing_details: Make the underlying space explicit for stand-alone use: the 2-dimensional family N = {N(μ,σ^2) | μ ∈ ℝ, σ > 0}, viewed with its statistical Lie-group structure.
State that left invariance is with respect to that specific Lie-group structure.

Clarify what "compatible with the Fisher metric" means in this problem; the FDIG item itself does not unpack the compatibility condition, so a stand-alone formulation should prevent confusion with ordinary Levi-Civita metric-compatibility.
Say whether the affine connections under consideration are required to be torsion-free; that is implicit from the surrounding statistical-manifold context but not explicit in the draft.
Specify the equivalence relation underlying the phrase "moduli space"; the paper uses the term here without defining exactly when two such left invariant connections are identified.
Keep the problem separate from the neighboring Section 1, item 3 question about left invariant semi-Riemannian metrics whose Levi-Civita connection is the exponential connection.
refined_question: Let N = {N(μ,σ^2) | μ ∈ ℝ, σ > 0} be the statistical Lie group of univariate normal distributions, equipped with its standard Lie-group structure and the Fisher metric g_F. Determine the moduli space of left invariant affine connections ∇ on N that are compatible with g_F in the information-geometric sense relevant here, namely those for which (N, g_F, ∇) is a left invariant statistical structure.
justification: The exact target is Section 1, item 1 under Jun-ichi Inoguchi. The nearby items show the same univariate-normal setting and distinguish this problem from a different one about Levi-Civita connections of left invariant semi-Riemannian metrics. Because the paper states the problem tersely, the refinement mainly makes the underlying model explicit and surfaces the implicit notions of compatibility and moduli without broadening the scope.
